subject: debugging a knitr bad request error

messages.author: 0315c305cb9f2470
messages.subject: debugging a knitr bad request error
parts:
Hi

 

I am trying to use knitr on knitr-examples/009-slides.Rmd from github and I keep getting this error:

Error in process_file(text, output) : 
  Quitting from lines 29-31: (009-slides.Rmd) Error : Bad Request

 

Calls: knit -> process_file
 
Execution halted
 
knitr terminated with status 1

 

Those lines correspond to a ggplot2 plot code chunk which works fine if I use it outside knitr.

 

I am running RStudio 0.96.331 on Windows and ggplot2 is installed with all the other packages (and loads fine when I run library(ggplot2))

 

> find.package('ggplot2')
[1] "C:/Program Files/R/R-2.15.1/library/ggplot2"

> packageVersion('knitr')

[1] ‘0.8’

> packageVersion('ggplot2')

[1] ‘0.9.2.1’

 

Any ideas what to try next?  I did just switch from Windows XP to Win 7 and started noticing this problem then, but am not sure that this is related.

 

Zach

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] debugging a knitr bad request error
parts:
Bad request is an indication of a web problem. I believe that is a
problem of Imgur, since I used the imgur_upload() function in the Rmd
document so that the plot can show up on Github:
https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/009-slides.md

Remove this line and it should work: opts_knit$set(upload.fun = imgur_upload)

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: c7ad2ad4911b43aa
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] debugging a knitr bad request error
parts:
Thanks for looking into this, Yihui. Creating html reports with knitr/Rmarkdown has become such an integral part of my workflow that it's very disruptive when something breaks down. 

For others out there who are running into this issue, I used the imguR package to implement the following workaround:

opts_knit$set(upload.fun = function(file, key = "60e9e47cff8483c6dc289a1cd674b40f") {
  res <- imguR::imguRupload(file, apikey = key)
  structure(res[["links.original"]], XML = res)
})

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] debugging a knitr bad request error
parts:
I spent another three hours digging into this problem, and I'm
relatively confident that this commit broke the upload function:

https://github.com/omegahat/RCurl/commit/b1f88c14e85893db10df8b264bc3ea2ec8085072#L8L120

It is unclear to me why .params was changed to lapply(.params, as,
"character") instead of as.list(.params), since the commit message
"writing chapter" was vague, but the consequence is that it breaks the
results from fileUpload(), e.g.

> library(RCurl)
> .params = list(file = fileUpload(file.path(R.home(), 'NEWS')))
> lapply(.params, as, "character")
$file
[1] "/usr/lib/R/NEWS" "character(0)" "character(0)"

> # it should really be this:
> .params
$file
$filename
[1] "/usr/lib/R/NEWS"

$contents
character(0)

$contentType
character(0)

attr(,"class")
[1] "FileUploadInfo"


It I revert that single change, postForm() will be able to upload
files again. However, even if I do that, there is still a problem
which I cannot figure out: the file seems to be uploaded twice. Here
is one of the results I got when I tried to upload an image to imgur
with knitr::imgur_upload():

The imguR package was apparently broken as well; its author gave up
postForm() and turned to Hadley's httr package for the POST() function
instead, which uses .postForm() instead of postForm()

I guess that is all I can do and explain at the moment; I really
cannot afford more time on this problem. I'll be grateful if Duncan
could offer some help.

>
> The change comes from a patch by somebody else that unfortunately
> was not as easy to apply or as informed as it might have been. But
> in an effort to aid that persons package, I applied the patch.
>
> The change in the current devel version is
>
> .params = lapply(.params,
> function(x)
> if(is.atomic(x))
> as.character(x)
> else
> x)
>
> which is as minimalistic and defensive as possible.
>
> That will be in the next release.
>
> So it is a shame you had to spend time wading through this.
>
